changes.summary: With the “100 Works that Tell the Climate Story” operation, the Musée d’Orsay invites you to take painters, sculptors and naturalists as your guides and rediscover these masterpieces from a new perspective. Housed in a train station where only electric trains arrived and departed in the 1900s, by its very nature the Musée d’Orsay is one of the venues that embody the history of modernity. The period covered by its collections (1848-1914) isn’t only marked by the rise of transport, but more generally by major technological acceleration, supported by massive use of coal and then of gas and oil. Artists were witnesses to these changes, revealing the modernization of the world, its rapid urbanization, as well as of the richness of its landscapes and its fauna and flora, whose fragility we can see all too well today. As you make your way through the rooms, as in any of the thirty or more museums across Metropolitan France, it’s up to you to spot the first clues to an ecological and climatic bifurcation whose effects on our environment are now unambiguously perceptible.
